Q: "Could not find main class" on .jar execution A:

The fact that double clicking is saying that it cannot find the main class means that a JRE is installed. That is NOT the problem.

It also means that a Windows shortcut and/or ".jar" file type binding exists. (It must exist because the error message is coming from the java command!) That is NOT the problem ... either.

The problem is (I think) that the JAR file has not been correctly created as an executable JAR file. An executable JAR file has a Main-class entry in its manifest that tells java.exe or javaw.exe which class contains the public static void main(String[]) method that is used to start the application.

Either the Main-class manifest entry is missing, or it refers to a non-existent class.

Since this is your program, you need to take a closer look at the way that you are creating the JAR file. You most likely need to tell NetBeans which class to use as the entry point / "main" class.

Q: I need help guys, A:

So you are writing a JavaScript to automate your task on Facebook, right? I would suggest you go the route of using officially supported API from Facebook:

https://developers.facebook.com/docs/graph-api

Reasons for using official API rather than writing your rudimentary JavaScript code by brute force:

  • Writing JavaScript code to interact with sites is actually a bot behavior.
  • Large social networking sites mostly block bot behavior, or at least make it very difficult. Facebook is no exception.
  • Even if you use tools like Selenium to make the bot-coding less painful and less error prone, in the eyes of those big techs it's still bot behavior nevertheless.
  • What's more: It's against their TOS. Your automatic bot script puts your account in danger of being blocked or even deleted.

So, using their approved API will get you much better performance, more reliable response, you get to read their official document to understand what particular features can fulfill your needs, and best of all, if you encounter a problem you know where to ask (Facebook support, of course).

Just my 2c.

Q: Bash - seamlessly run scripts with CRLF line endings A:

I used

sudo ln -s /usr/bin/perl $'/usr/bin/perl\r'

to create the interpreter link. The result is shown with ls like

'/usr/bin/perl'$'\r' -> /usr/bin/perl

Albeit looking a bit strange, this works flawlessly with the many scripts which I brought over from windows and spares the need for any conversion or other workarounds which one always has to do and think of again and again.

Q: How to make dedicated Azure Event Hub cluster zone redundant? A:

As far as I can see terraform's azurerm provider does not support zone redundant event hub cluster. You can use Terraform Az API Provider and Microsoft.EventHub/clusters@2026-01-01 type to set zoneRedundant property to true upon deployment. After which you will have zone redundant Event Hub cluster.:
